en: Itivuttaka 29 Dukanipāta, Paṭhamavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. These, monks, are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is superior to the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far better than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me:

"Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more excellent than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more sublime than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more distinguished than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more noble than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more preeminent than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more supreme than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more unsurpassed than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more peerless than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more incomparable than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more matchless than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more unequaled than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more unparallelled than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more unrivaled than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more without equal than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more without a second than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more without a counterpart than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so heard by me: "Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who delights in the Dhamma and the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Of these two, monks, the person who delights in the Dhamma is far more without a rival than the person who does not delight in the Dhamma. Thus it was said by
The Discourse on Dwelling in Happiness.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with two qualities dwells happily in this very life, without vexation, without despair, and without fever.
With the breakup of the body, after death, a happy destination is to be expected.
By what two factors?
By guarding the doors of the sense faculties and by moderation in eating.
“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these two qualities dwells happily in this very life— without vexation, without despair, and without fever—
and after the breakup of the body, after death, a happy destination is to be expected.
Thus the Blessed One spoke.
In this regard, it is said:
“The eye, the ear, and the nose,
the tongue, the body, and likewise the mind;”
For that monk whose doors are well-guarded,
and who knows the proper measure in food—
And being restrained in the sense faculties,
he attains bodily happiness and mental happiness— true happiness indeed.
With a body not burning and with a mind not burning,
whether by day or by night,
“Such a one dwells in happiness.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The second [sutta].
